'''Igor Olshansky'''{{efn|{{langx|uk|Ігор Ольшанський|{{transliteration|uk|ukrainian|Ihor Olshanskyi}}}}}} ({{IPAc-en|oʊ|l|ˈ|ʃ|æ|n|s|k|i}}; born 3 May 1982) is a former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]] and was selected by the [[San Diego Chargers]] in the second round of the [[2004 NFL draft]]. He also played for the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and [[Miami Dolphins]].

He is the first Ukrainian to play in the NFL, and the first born in the [[Soviet Union]] to do so.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ditrani|first=Vinny|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-record-looking-out-for-no-1/166646137/|title=Looking out for No. 1|newspaper=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 23, 2004|access-date=February 25, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Dubow|first=Josh|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-monitor-draft-sleeper--cou/166646156/|title=Draft sleeper: Ukrainian could be first-round pick|newspaper=[[The Monitor (Texas)|The Monitor]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 22, 2004|access-date=February 25, 2025}}</ref>

'''Elbert L. "Ickey" Woods''' (born February 28, 1966) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1988 through 1991. He played [[college football]] for the [[UNLV Rebels football|UNLV Rebels]]. He is best remembered for his "[[Ickey Shuffle]]" end zone dance, performed each time he scored a [[touchdown]]. After a [[rookie]] season in which he set numerous rookie franchise records, a series of injuries shortened his NFL career and he retired after four years.

'''Hunter Dwight Smith''' (born August 9, 1977) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Punter (American football)|punter]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the seventh round of the [[1999 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1999 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1999/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>  He played [[college football]] for the [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame Fighting Irish]].

Smith earned a [[Super Bowl ring]] with the Colts in [[Super Bowl XLI]] as they beat the [[Chicago Bears]]. He is currently the representative for House District 24 of the [[Indiana House of Representatives]].<ref name=IS>{{cite web |last=Carloni |first=Brittany |title= Former Colts punter Hunter Smith launches Statehouse bid |url=https://www.indystar.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/11/05/indiana-results-election-winners-contested-central-indiana-statehouse-races/75847704007/?tbref=hp|work=[[The Indianapolis Star]] |date=November 5, 2024}}</ref>

'''Ian Maurice Gold''' (born August 23, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who played as a [[linebacker]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played for the [[Denver Broncos]] from [[2000 Denver Broncos season|2000]] to [[2003 Denver Broncos season|2003]] and [[2004 Denver Broncos season|2004]] to [[2007 Denver Broncos season|2007]] and for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in [[2004 Tampa Bay Buccaneers season|2004]]. He appeared in 115 NFL games, 80 as a starter, registered 422 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]], and was selected to play in the [[2002 Pro Bowl]].

Gold played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] from [[1996 Michigan Wolverines football team|1996]] to [[1999 Michigan Wolverines football team|1999]] and was a member of the undefeated [[1997 Michigan Wolverines football team]] that was ranked #1 in the final [[AP Poll]]. He was selected as a first-team linebacker on both the [[1998 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1998]] and [[1999 All-Big Ten Conference football team|1999 All-Big Ten teams]].

Smart played 4 seasons for [[BC Lions]] and replaced [[Aaron Lockett (gridiron football)|Aaron Lockett]] as their kick returner during the 2006 season. He became their backup running back when [[Alexis Bwenge]] became a [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]]. Smart scored a 25-yard touchdown as running back for the BC Lions in their [[94th Grey Cup|2006 Grey Cup]] victory.
